name: Caremark

subjectOf.text: In In re Citigroup the Delaware Court of Chancery refused to extend the Caremark oversight duty, which concerns monitoring for illegal conduct, into oversight liability for business risk, so an inability to predict the future and an incorrect evaluation of business risk are not breaches of a director's oversight responsibilities.
subjectOf.abstract: under the Caremark line of cases would 133 not be extended to impose oversight liability for business risk
subjectOf.citation: Painter and Kaal, Initial Reflections on an Evolving Standard Constraints on Risk Taking by Directors and Officers in (2010). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1558614
scope_conditions: Delaware law; derivative claims premised on subprime exposure
oversight liability requires showing the directors knew they were not discharging their duties or consciously disregarded them

subjectOf.text: The liability standard for breach of fiduciary duty is set so high that courts rarely find directors in violation, because only a board's sustained or systematic failure to exercise oversight can produce liability.
subjectOf.abstract: The standard for liability is so high that it is hard for courts to find directors in violation of their fiduciary duties.2 Only a board's sustained or systematic failure to exercise oversight can result in liability.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Elizabeth R. Malay, The Role of Corporate Integrity Agreements in the Expansion of Fiduciary Duties (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2317580
scope_conditions: director oversight liability under Caremark and its progeny

subjectOf.text: The contractual obligations contained in CIAs can enhance directors' default fiduciary duties, expanding the duty of care for directors of health care corporations beyond the legal standard set by Caremark and Stone v. Ritter.
subjectOf.abstract: The contractual obligations in CIAs can enhance directors' fiduciary default duties, expanding the duty of care for directors of health care corporations beyond the legal standard under Caremark and Ritter.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Elizabeth R. Malay, The Role of Corporate Integrity Agreements in the Expansion of Fiduciary Duties (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2317580
scope_conditions: directors of health care corporations operating under an executed CIA

subjectOf.text: Outside the CIA context, oversight claims are the most difficult theory in corporation law on which to win judgment, and courts dismiss duty of care cases routinely at the pleading stage.
subjectOf.abstract: Courts dismiss duty of care cases routinely at the pleading stage.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Elizabeth R. Malay, The Role of Corporate Integrity Agreements in the Expansion of Fiduciary Duties (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2317580
scope_conditions: derivative suits alleging lack of oversight

subjectOf.text: Under Delaware law as applied in In re Citigroup, directors' incorrect evaluation of business risk and their inability to predict the future do not violate the duty of oversight, so the Caremark duty to monitor is not extended to business risk.
subjectOf.abstract: According to the Delaware Chancery court, directors' incorrect evaluation of business risk and their inability to predict the future did not violate directors' duty of oversight.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, A Comparative Perspective on the Limitations of the Duty of Oversight – A Comment on Lisa Fairfax (2013)
scope_conditions: claims framed as failures to monitor business risk
